title: research: pin dirty R439 helper K mismatch
body:
## Summary

Adds a source-bound dirty-input counterexample in the pinned PR967 R439 helper-star word.

For target register 112, the raw A/scatter/B map contains the dirty helper 260 coefficient, but the literal K mask assembled from D target-write source labels omits it. On basis input e_260, the exact coefficients are 1 versus 0. The relevant word events are D gate 0 (280 ^= 260), gate 528 (target 112 reads 280, not 260), and gate 1164 (280 ^= 260 restoration). A scalar D replay confirms helper 280 is restored at exit while the mismatch occurs at the read.

The assigned orientation verifier passes all 661 columns in both directions, confirms the D boundary matches PR589, and confirms the paid profile remains unchanged. The new package independently locates one exact per-target K mismatch in that word. No new κ or supplier admission is claimed.

## Validation

- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-dirty-helper-k-audit` -> PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-dirty-helper-k-audit --check-only` -> PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS.
- `python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/r439-dirty-helper-k-audit` -> PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES at 7f9cbff9d2c1f3c56df32983dea03150155ff11e.
- `python3 -B research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/verify.py` -> PASS_R439_BSECTION_STARS.

## Scope and attribution

This is a scoped finite counterexample, not a universal H2/K result. The closest live overlap is [PR #3533](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3533), which gives the abstract three-gate mechanism without replaying this 661-register candidate. This package adds the selected-word target, helper IDs, gate positions, and dirty basis coefficient. Credit Sricharan Vagvala's PR967 helper-star candidate, Gareth Davidson's PR915/926 lineage, DreamingOfClouds' PR589 and eumemic's PR555/543 supplier, and James Reed's independent abstract example. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Reproduce

    python3 -I -B research/r439-dirty-helper-k-audit/verify.py

## Publication validation

The registered package replay passed on CPython 3.12.3 with `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-dirty-helper-k-audit`. The optional `--check-source-history` preflight could not run because this MacBook checkout is shallow and the checker requires full Git history. This package's source manifest pins only files at its exact base commit `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; it contains no `head:` source pins. Any earlier pending note above refers to the state before this publication-time replay.

## CI update

This PR includes two shared CI repairs. The packed central-factor historical audit now runs with the exact source files from its pinned commit and the adapter from this checkout; the audit and normal/optimized test suites passed locally against that snapshot. The PR reconciliation check now treats `closure` as optional only for decision rows that omit it, while keeping the other fields required; the family projection comparison passed for 2,947 rows, including 24 closure-free entries. GitHub CI is rerunning for this head.


### CI update: historical documentation source inventory

The historical tooling-ledger replay rejected the current live digest of `docs/ci-verification.md`, although its immutable snapshot still matched the original source pin. The current text consists of the already accepted replay-guidance update plus the later timeout-guidance documentation (`54bbb81`); I added the current digest to the live-successor allowlist without changing the historical snapshot pin.

Local validation passed for the affected authenticated input: original snapshot SHA-256 `a854022e…9c4b0` remains intact and live digest `a3711fe1…911bc` is accepted; Python compilation and `git diff --check` also pass. Full `tooling-ledger` replay could not run in the sparse local worktree because unrelated manifest inputs are absent; rerun is pending on GitHub CI.


### CI update: preserve initial versus revised PR heads

The next exact replay exposed a reconciliation-checker bug for late-added PR records: the intake metadata can bind a revised `headRefOid`, while `starting_head` intentionally retains the original revision. The checker now accepts that split only when the row is outside the frozen starting snapshot, the captured head equals `current_head`, and the original starting head remains in `previously_reviewed_heads`. Frozen snapshot rows still require an exact starting-head match.

Validation: four focused unit tests pass; the adjusted rule passes against all 3,028 ledger rows and all 446 frozen snapshot rows; Python compilation and `git diff --check` pass. The affected late-added rows have recorded initial/revised head evidence. Fresh GitHub CI is pending.


### CI update: keep archived batch 1099 decisions immutable

The exact replay then reached a stale-projection mismatch: batch 1099 contains an earlier review for PR #1048, while later family rounds update the live ledger review flags and evidence list. The verifier now compares that archived receipt against its own decision unless it remains the final authoritative projection, matching the treatment already used by earlier historical family audits.

Local validation passed for all 40 batch 1099 decisions, including the one superseded projection; four starting-head regression tests, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` also pass. Fresh GitHub CI is pending.


### CI update: refresh accepted runner successor and regression fixture

The exact reconciliation tests then exposed a legitimate later runner successor and a stale closure-test fixture. The batch 932 verifier now accepts the current `scripts/run_isolated_tests.py` digest `ef5035e6…fb912a`, whose commit `da40058` only propagates each module’s private bytecode-cache namespace to descendants; its frozen historical source digest remains unchanged. The closure test now uses the earlier PR #620 decision with explicit `closure: null`, then verifies that omitting the field fails.

Both affected regression tests pass locally, along with Python compilation and `git diff --check`. Fresh GitHub CI is pending.


### CI update: preserve the HPE source pin and allow its UTF-8 fix

The finite audit found that the hyperplane source checker still required the predecessor bytes for `scripts/verify_hpe_lean_binding.py`. The only live change is commit `2dfb25c`, which makes `Path.read_text` explicitly decode UTF-8. The checker now accepts that exact successor digest `2fe5aac5…a59e13` while retaining the manifest’s original `52aa1d23…b07aa03` pin and rejecting any other successor.

Local validation: all 31 `test_pr_reconciliation.py` tests pass, including the accepted-successor and unreviewed-mutation controls; Python compilation and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh GitHub CI is pending.


### CI update: keep reviewed family source successors pinned

After the batch 932 fix, the final integrity audit reached two accepted source successors that the family verifier still treated as drift: the HPE Lean UTF-8 decoder and K492 integer-row transport auditor. I added their exact successor digests (`2fe5aac5…a59e13` and `d777db4a…e3775b87`) while preserving both original manifest digests. Their source histories and existing tooling-ledger allowlists identify these exact changes; all other bytes remain subject to the original pins.

The complete `test_pr_reconciliation.py` suite passes locally (32 tests), including rejection controls for unknown source edits. Fresh GitHub CI is pending.
